Emperor penguins live in Antarctica, one of the coldest places on Earth. In winter, the temperature can fall below minus forty degrees. To stay warm, the penguins stand very close together in a large group. They take turns standing at the outside of the group, where it is coldest, and then move slowly to the warm middle. In this way, no penguin has to stay in the cold for too long. The fathers also keep an egg on their feet under a warm fold of skin for about two months while the mothers are away looking for food. This teamwork helps the baby penguins to be born safely.

options.text: How fathers and mothers choose their names
Where penguins find food in the summer
How penguins work together to survive the cold
Why Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth

The word comes from an Arabic word that means “season.” Warm, wet winds blow from the ocean toward the land, and the sky stays gray for weeks. For farmers, the rain is a gift because rice needs a lot of water to grow. However, too much rain can cause floods that damage houses and roads. People prepare by cleaning drains, keeping an umbrella ready, and checking weather reports every day. Children often enjoy the season too. They jump in puddles and listen to the sound of rain on the roof.

What can too much rain cause?

options.text: Strong winds that blow the roofs off
Drains that slowly start to grow rice
Floods that damage houses and roads

To warn that they contain much sugar
To list the drinks that doctors sell here

The principal said the idea was worth trying.

Which dish did only a few students like?

Many people think of failure as the opposite of success, but it is often a step toward it. A gardener who grows nothing in the first year learns which soil is too dry. A runner who stops halfway learns how to pace herself. Even a scientist whose experiment fails gains useful information, because now she knows one more thing that does not work. Of course, failure is never fun. It stings, and it can make us want to quit. Yet those who keep trying and think carefully about each mistake are the ones who finally find a way forward.

To explain how to study for exams

questions.prompt:

questions.prompt: "The year ___ the war ended is remembered in every history book." Choose the best word.

questions.explanation: year는 시간을 나타내는 선행사라서 관계부사 when을 써요.

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: reason을 선행사로 하는 관계부사는 why예요.

questions.prompt: In "I doubt that he will come," the clause "that he will come" works as...

questions.prompt: "This is the lab where they test new batteries." Which phrase can replace "where" without changing the meaning?

questions.explanation: where = 전치사 + which예요. which만 쓰면 전치사 in이 빠져 틀려요.

questions.prompt: "Where does Mina live?" Which sentence reports this question correctly?

questions.explanation: ‘~인지 아닌지’를 뜻하는 명사절은 whether로 이끌어요. 나머지는 뒤의 절이 완전해서 알맞지 않아요.

questions.explanation: I knew that she would call에서 that은 knew의 목적어절을 이끌어요. 나머지는 지시어이거나 관계대명사예요.

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: afraid 뒤에서 말하는 내용을 이끄는 접속사는 that이에요.

questions.explanation: 감정 형용사 pleased 뒤에 이유를 나타내는 that절이 와요.

questions.prompt:

questions.explanation: decide는 ‘무엇을’ 결정하는지를 목적어로 취하고, whether절이 그 목적어 역할을 해요.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.

questions.explanation: Weather permitting은 ‘날씨가 허락하면’이라는 조건이에요. unless는 반대 뜻이 돼요.

questions.prompt: “The meeting being over, everyone went home.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?

options.text: Although the meeting was over, everyone stayed there.
While the meeting is over, everyone went home.
After the meeting was over, everyone went home.
Before the meeting was over, everyone went home.

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 독립분사구문 The meeting being over는 ‘회의가 끝난 뒤(끝났으므로)’의 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: “Having no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.”와 같은 뜻의 문장은?

options.text: If he has no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.
Although he had no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.
After he talked to everyone, Daeho felt lonely.
Since he had no one to talk to, Daeho felt lonely.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Having no one ~은 이유를 나타내므로 Since/Because를 써서 바꿔요.

questions.prompt: “Being a doctor, she knows how to treat a fever.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: ‘의사이기 때문에’ 열을 치료할 줄 안다는 뜻이므로 이유예요.

questions.prompt: “The train left at six, arriving in Daegu at nine.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 문장 뒤에 오는 -ing는 ‘그리고 ~했다’처럼 이어지는 결과나 연속 동작을 나타내요.

questions.prompt: “Reaching the top of the hill, we sat down to rest.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: ‘언덕 꼭대기에 닿았을 때’라는 뜻의 시간이에요.

questions.prompt: “Left in direct sunlight, chocolate melts quickly.”에서 분사구문이 나타내는 의미는?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: ‘햇빛에 그대로 두면’이라는 뜻이므로 조건이에요.

questions.prompt: 다음 중 분사구문이 양보(~이지만)의 뜻을 나타내는 문장은?

options.text: Opening the box, Tom began to smile.
Turning off the light, you can save energy.
Feeling dizzy, Rina sat down at once.
Living near the sea, Dan can't swim.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 바다 근처에 살지만 수영을 못한다는 뜻이라 양보예요. 나머지는 각각 이유, 시간, 조건에 가까워요.

questions.prompt: “Driving to work, ___.” 빈칸에 알맞은 절은?

options.text: a strange noise came from the engine
the engine made a strange noise for him
Dad heard a strange noise from the engine
it was noisy from the engine

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Driving의 의미상 주어는 사람이어야 해요. 엔진이나 소리는 운전할 수 없으므로 나머지는 틀려요.

questions.prompt: “Climbing the mountain, ___.” 빈칸에 알맞은 절은?

options.text: a lovely view appeared before our eyes
the weather made it very hard
the trail seemed shorter to us
the hikers enjoyed a lovely view

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: ‘올라가는’ 주체가 주절의 주어여야 해요. 보기 중 hikers만 산을 오를 수 있어요.

questions.prompt: “Having eaten too much, ___.” 빈칸에 알맞은 절은?

options.text: I felt sick for the whole evening
the greasy pizza made me feel quite sick
a bad stomachache began very quickly
my stomach started to hurt badly

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 먹은 사람이 주절의 주어여야 해요. 피자, 복통, 배는 ‘먹은’ 주체가 될 수 없어요.

questions.prompt: 분사구문의 의미상 주어가 어색한 문장은?

options.text: Reading in bed, the lamp suddenly went out.
Waiting for the bus, I checked my phone.
Surprised by the noise, the baby started to cry.
Having lost his keys, Joon had to call his mother.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Reading의 주체는 사람인데 주절의 주어는 the lamp라서 어색해요(현수 분사구문).

questions.prompt: 분사구문의 주어가 주절의 주어와 맞지 않아 어색한 문장은?

options.text: Lost in the forest, the children stayed calm.
Having cleaned the room, Ella took a short rest.
Stuck in the elevator, the lights went out.
Surprised by the result, the team cheered loudly.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: ‘갇힌’ 것은 the lights가 아니라 사람이어야 해요.

questions.prompt: “Running for the bus, my bag fell off my shoulder.”를 바르게 고친 문장은?

options.text: Having run for the bus, my bag fell off my shoulder.
As I ran for the bus, my bag fell off my shoulder.
Ran for the bus, my bag fell off my shoulder.
Running for the bus, my bag was falling off my shoulder.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 가방은 달릴 수 없으므로 분사구문의 주어가 어긋나요. 절로 풀어 쓰면 해결돼요.

questions.prompt: 분사구문의 주어가 주절의 주어와 달라도 맞는 문장은?

options.text: Having set, the park became quiet.
The sun having set, the park became quiet.
The sun have set, the park became quiet.
The sun set, the park became quiet.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 주어가 다르면 분사 앞에 주어를 남겨요(독립분사구문). 나머지는 주어가 어긋나거나 동사 형태가 틀려요.

questions.prompt: 분사구문으로 바꿀 때 종속절의 주어를 지울 수 없는 문장은?

options.text: After I finished lunch, I took a walk.
As Hana was kind, everyone liked her.
When she saw the snake, she screamed.
Because he was sleepy, he went to bed.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 종속절과 주절의 주어가 다르면(Hana / everyone) 주어를 남겨서 독립분사구문으로 써야 해요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
___ in a hurry, the report had many mistakes.

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 보고서는 ‘쓰인’ 수동 관계이므로 Written이에요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The boys ran across the field, ___ at the top of their voices.
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 뒤에 붙는 동시 동작은 -ing로 나타내요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The man ___ at the gate is our new neighbor.

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미며 ‘기다리고 있는’ 능동 관계이므로 -ing예요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The letter ___ yesterday has not arrived yet.
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.

questions.explanation: 편지는 ‘보내진’ 수동 관계이므로 과거분사 sent예요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?

questions.explanation: 아이들이 놀람을 ‘느끼는’ 쪽이므로 과거분사 amazed예요.

questions.explanation: with + 목적어 + 분사: 불이 ‘꺼진’ 수동 관계이므로 과거분사를 써요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
She kept walking with her dog ___ behind her.
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 개가 ‘따라오는’ 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 following이에요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
___ no reply, Kim sent a second message.
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Kim이 ‘받지 못한’ 능동 관계의 분사구문이므로 Getting이에요.

questions.prompt:
빈칸에 알맞은 것은?
The first prize, ___ by a ten-year-old girl, surprised everyone.

questions.explanation: Ben이 음악을 ‘듣는’ 것은 능동(Listening), 음악 때문에 ‘방해받는’ 것은 수동(Disturbed)이에요.

questions.prompt: “그는 눈을 감은 채 노래를 불렀다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

questions.explanation: with + 목적어 + 과거분사: 눈은 ‘감겨진’ 상태예요.

questions.prompt: “그녀는 다리를 꼰 채 앉아 있었다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

options.text: She was sitting with her legs crosses.

She was sitting with her legs crossed.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 다리는 ‘꼬인’ 상태이므로 수동 관계의 과거분사 crossed를 써요.

questions.prompt: “그 소년은 편지를 읽는 동안 울었다.”(동시 동작)를 나타내는 문장은?

Having been read the letter, the boy cried.

보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 동시에 일어난 일은 -ing로 나타내요. Having read는 ‘읽은 뒤에’라는 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: “Because Tom had not studied, he failed the test.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 바꾼 것은?

options.text: Not to have studied, Tom failed the test.
Not having study, Tom failed the test.
Not having studied, Tom failed the test.
Not studied, Tom failed the test.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 먼저 일어난 일의 부정은 Not having + 과거분사로 써요.

questions.prompt: “Having bought the tickets, Jenny went to the cinema.”에서 일어난 순서는?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 완료 분사구문(Having + 과거분사)은 주절보다 먼저 일어난 일을 나타내요.

questions.prompt: “Generally speaking, summers in Korea are hot and humid.”에서 Generally speaking과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 표현은?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Generally speaking은 ‘일반적으로’라는 뜻으로 In general과 같아요.

questions.prompt: “Judging from his accent, he must be from the south.”에서 Judging from의 뜻은?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Judging from ~은 ‘~로 판단하면’이라는 뜻의 관용 표현이에요.

questions.prompt: “Considering her age, she plays the violin very well.”에서 Considering의 뜻은?
hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Considering ~은 ‘~을 고려하면, ~치고는’이라는 뜻이에요.

questions.prompt: 분사구문의 부정형이 틀린 문장은?

questions.explanation: 분사구문에서는 do동사를 쓰지 않고 Not + -ing로 써요.

questions.prompt: 완료 분사구문이 틀린 문장은?

options.text: Having been praised by the coach, Lee smiled.
Having cooked dinner, Mom called us to the table.
Having overslept, Tim missed the first bus.
Having ate lunch, Sam went back to work.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: Having 뒤에는 과거분사가 와야 해요. ate가 아니라 eaten이에요.

questions.prompt: with + 목적어 + 분사 구문이 틀린 문장은?

options.text: Tom sat with his arms folded.
The cat sat by the door with its ears pointing up.
Mia walked with her hair blowing in the wind.
My brother stood at the door with his shoes taking off.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 신발은 ‘벗겨진’ 수동 관계이므로 with his shoes off 또는 taken off가 맞아요.

questions.prompt: 수동 의미의 분사구문이 올바르게 쓰인 문장은?

options.text: Written by a famous poet, I enjoyed this poem very much.

Written by a famous poet, this poem is loved by many.
Writes by a famous poet, this poem is loved by many.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: ‘쓰인’ 것은 시이므로 주절의 주어도 this poem이어야 해요. 'Written by a famous poet, I enjoyed this poem very much.'는 주어가 I라서 틀려요.

questions.prompt: “창밖을 바라보며 그는 한숨을 쉬었다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

options.text: Looking out the window, a sigh was heard.

Looking out the window, he sighed.
Looked out the window, he sighed.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 동시 동작은 -ing 분사구문으로 나타내요. 주어(he)와 분사의 의미상 주어가 일치해야 해요.

questions.prompt: “그녀는 음악을 들으며 숙제를 했다.”를 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

options.text: She did her homework listening to music.
She did her homework to listening to music.
She did her homework listen to music.
She did her homework listened to music.

hints: 문제를 천천히 다시 읽어 보세요.
보기를 하나씩 문제에 넣어 확인해 보세요.
questions.explanation: 문장 뒤에 -ing를 붙이면 ‘~하면서’라는 동시 동작을 나타낼 수 있어요.

questions.prompt: “그는 방을 나가면서 뒤로 문을 닫았다.”를 분사구문으로 바르게 옮긴 것은?

options.text: He left the room, closing the door behind him.

Hanji is a traditional Korean paper made from the inner bark of the mulberry tree. Making it by hand takes many steps. First, the bark is boiled and beaten until it turns into soft fibers. Mixed with water and a natural plant glue, these fibers are scooped onto a screen and shaken gently, forming a thin, even sheet. Dried in the sun, the sheets become strong yet light. questions.prompt:
Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support about a quarter of all sea life. Built slowly by tiny animals called corals, a reef can take thousands of years to form. The corals live together with algae, which give them food and bright colors. When the water becomes too warm, stressed corals push out the algae and turn white, a process called bleaching. Bleached reefs are not dead, but they are weak. Given enough time and cooler water, they can recover. Unfortunately, warming seas, polluted rivers, and careless tourists, touching or breaking the coral, make recovery difficult in many places. Protecting reefs therefore requires action at local and global levels.

Warm weather is the true cause of tiredness.

questions.prompt:
Our school's reading club meets every Thursday after lunch. Whoever wants to join is welcome, whatever grade they are in. Last month, however, we faced a problem: some members read quickly, whereas others needed more time, so discussions often felt uneven. Our advisor, Ms. Park, suggested a simple rule. Whichever book the group picks, each member reads only one section carefully and then explains it to everyone else. At first, several students worried that they would forget details. Even so, the plan worked well. Now the quiet readers speak confidently, and the fast readers listen more patiently. No matter how busy the week is, nearly everyone comes to the meeting, because it has become the most relaxed part of the school day.

What is the passage mainly about?

options.text: A new rule that made a school club run better
What students should bring to a Thursday meeting
How a teacher chose the most popular book of the year
Why fast readers should avoid group discussions

Whenever the rain eases, they run to the lake with their fishing rods, and whoever catches the first fish gets to choose dinner. So far, nobody has caught anything, yet we keep laughing. options.text: To share news about her trip so far
To invite Dana to join the cabin trip tomorrow
To complain about the cabin and the food
To ask Dana for help with a fishing game

questions.prompt:
Many families struggle with phones at the dinner table. Whoever has tried a no-phone rule knows it is harder than it sounds. Although most people agree that talking together is healthy, the urge to check messages is strong. One family in our neighborhood found a clever solution. Whenever dinner begins, everyone drops their phone into a basket by the door. Whoever reaches for it first must wash the dishes. At first, the children complained; however, within two weeks the habit felt natural. Their father says dinners now last twice as long, and nobody minds. No matter how interesting an online message seems, it can wait until dessert is over. The basket, it seems, has become the quietest hero of the house.

What is the main point of the passage?

options.text: Children complain whenever parents make new rules.
A basket rule helped one family enjoy dinner.
Washing dishes is the best punishment at home.
Phones should be banned in every public restaurant.

questions.prompt:
Students often believe that staying up late is the best way to prepare for an exam. However, sleep researchers disagree. Whatever you study at night, your brain needs rest to store it. Even if you read the whole textbook twice, a tired memory works poorly the next morning. In a small school project, two groups of students learned the same word list. One group slept eight hours, whereas the other stayed awake all night. The sleepers remembered far more words, no matter how hard the others had tried. Of course, a good plan matters too. Whichever subject is hardest, study it earlier in the day, and keep the last hour before bed calm.

What is the main message of the passage?

options.text: Reading a textbook twice wastes time.
Late-night study is the best exam plan.
Short word lists are easier for students.

Cooks should taste and adjust as they go.
Grandmothers always know more than recipe books.
Ovens are the most important tool in a kitchen.

Smartphones will soon replace all language teachers.
Apps are useful, but real conversation matters too.

questions.prompt:
My violin teacher once told me, "Whatever you play, play it slowly first." I did not understand until my last recital. For weeks I had rushed through the hard passages, hoping speed would hide my mistakes. Whenever I performed in front of my family, the same notes went wrong. Then I followed her advice and practised each bar at half speed, however boring it felt. Slowly, my fingers learned the shape of the music. At the recital, my hands were shaking, but they remembered what to do. I did not play perfectly, whereas the girl before me did. Still, I walked off the stage smiling, because I knew exactly why each note sounded the way it did.

What is the passage mainly about?

options.text: A recital is easier than practice at home.
The teacher stopped the writer's lessons.
Slow practice made the writer play better.
Playing quickly is the secret of good music.

questions.prompt:
Traditional Korean houses were heated by ondol, a system that warms the floor instead of the air. Smoke and hot air from a fireplace in the kitchen traveled through channels under stone slabs, and the stones kept the heat for hours. As a result, people sat and slept on the floor, and the furniture was low and light. In summer, however, the same houses stayed cool because the main hall had a wooden floor that let breezes pass underneath. This combination of two floors shows how builders solved the problem of very different seasons. Today, modern apartments use hot-water pipes in place of smoke channels, but the idea of a warm floor remains the same.

How did the ondol system heat a room?

options.text: Heated water ran through clay pipes built inside the walls of each room.
Hot air from the kitchen fire warmed the stones under the floor.
A stove in the middle of the room warmed the air.

questions.prompt:
In some cities, you can borrow a drill, a tent or a sewing machine from a 'library of things'. The idea is simple: most households use such objects only a few times a year, yet each one must buy its own. By sharing, a neighborhood can reduce spending and also reduce waste, since fewer items need to be manufactured. Members pay a small fee, return the items on time and care for them as if they were their own. Not everything about the system is easy, however. Volunteers must repair damaged tools, and popular items are often unavailable on weekends. Even so, the libraries are growing, perhaps because they offer something modern shopping rarely does: a chance to meet your neighbors.

Why do the libraries make economic sense?

options.text: Tools wear out if they are not used.
Manufacturers give the objects for free.
Neighbors prefer to pay higher fees.
People rarely use many household items.

The editors forgot to write it.
The file had been saved under another name.

To study the cold climate of the north

To keep backup copies of the world's crop seeds

Winds over the sea are stronger and steadier than those on land, so each turbine produces more electricity. In addition, there are few buildings to block the view, which reduces complaints from residents. On the other hand, building at sea is expensive: the towers need strong foundations, and workers must travel by boat for repairs. Fishermen also worry that the structures will take up good fishing grounds. Engineers respond that the foundations can become homes for shellfish and small fish, and some wind farms already permit fishing between the towers. Whether the benefits outweigh the costs will depend on careful planning for each location.

Why do offshore turbines produce more electricity?

options.text: Fishermen help to keep them running.
The towers at sea are always taller.
The winds at sea are stronger and steadier.
There is more sunshine over the water.

Teachers do not read the answers.
Students do not get enough sleep.

They hold on with many tiny tube feet

A teacher in a language school asked her students to learn ten common expressions in two ways: half of the class read them from a list, while the other half sang them to a simple tune. Meanwhile, she recommends that students try music as one tool among many, not as a replacement for regular practice.

The best songs for beginners to study in English class
How teachers should choose students for a class choir
A small experiment on learning expressions through singing

Scientists use the word "microplastics" for plastic fragments smaller than five millimeters. Some are made that small on purpose, such as the beads once added to certain face scrubs. Others form slowly as larger items, including bottles, bags, and fishing nets, break down in sunlight and waves. Washing synthetic clothing also releases tiny fibers that pass through household drains. Because the pieces are so small, they are hard to remove from water, and they can be swallowed by animals at every level of the food chain, from plankton to fish. Researchers are still investigating whether the particles harm human health, and results so far are mixed. Even so, many countries have limited the sale of products containing plastic beads, and some manufacturers now sell washing machine filters that trap fibers. These steps will not solve the problem alone, but they show that practical solutions exist.

Paper bags that dissolve in the rain
Synthetic clothing that is washed at home

Scientists use the word "microplastics" for plastic fragments smaller than five millimeters. Some are made that small on purpose, such as the beads once added to certain face scrubs. Others form slowly as larger items, including bottles, bags, and fishing nets, break down in sunlight and waves. Washing synthetic clothing also releases tiny fibers that pass through household drains. Because the pieces are so small, they are hard to remove from water, and they can be swallowed by animals at every level of the food chain, from plankton to fish. Researchers are still investigating whether the particles harm human health, and results so far are mixed. Even so, many countries have limited the sale of products containing plastic beads, and some manufacturers now sell washing machine filters that trap fibers. These steps will not solve the problem alone, but they show that practical solutions exist.

Why are microplastics hard to remove from water?

options.text: They sink to the bottom of the sea
They are hidden inside fishing nets
They dissolve completely in salt water

questions.prompt:
Most people have sent a message that autocorrect has turned into nonsense, but the feature does far more good than harm. Behind the scenes, the software compares what you type with a large list of words, estimates which word you probably meant, and replaces the error before you press send. Modern versions also learn from your habits: they remember the names of your friends, the slang you use, and the phrases you often repeat. The system is not perfect, because it cannot read your mind and it sometimes mistakes a rare word for a mistake. Experts therefore advise users to read quickly before sending any important message. Recyclers run out of clean water.
Its fibers become shorter each time.
